**TL;DR**

- **A violent unwind of the AI trade, plus an oil shock.** Nasdaq Composite **-2.60%** to 26,008.86 — its **steepest daily drop since early June** (Reuters). S&P 500 **-1.21%** to 7,663.43.
- Dow **+0.02%**, Russell 2000 **+0.11%**. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell **6.3%**, its biggest drop since 23 June.
- **Two shocks, same day.** (1) Meta's results — a beat — triggered an AI-capex scare:
- the stock printed its **first cash outflow in more than a decade** and announced **non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital for AI**;
- META closed **-6.98%**, reversing yesterday's +6.08% after-hours gain almost point for point.
- (2) **Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi targets** and a report said the US and Israel may resume strikes on Iran next month — crude to a five-month high.
- **Rates broke the other way.** The 10-year fell **19.3bp to 4.953%**, its first sub-5% close in a month. Bull-flattening led by duration; TLT +1.87%.
- VIX **+14.08% to 19.03** (intraday 20.31), VXN +17.61% to 28.72.
- **The rotation was real and heavily traded.** Equal-weight S&P (RSP) **+0.73% on 184% of average volume** while SPY fell 1.18%.
- Consumer staples led at **XLP +3.31% on 203% of volume**; utilities +2.07%, health care +1.32%. **Technology was last, XLK -3.29%.** Six of eleven sectors rose.
- **Two idiosyncratic shocks worth isolating:** **Moderna -17.57%** after partial Phase 3 cancer-vaccine data leaked online and was pulled (LULD halt at 12:34 ET;
- full data released later looked positive), and **Nokia -14.81%** on a free-cash-flow guidance cut despite beating.
- **After-hours:** **RHI +11.5%**, **DECK -8.7%**, **FIX -6.2%**, **VRSN -5.1%**, **BE -4.5%**. WDC reported at the close and is -1.2% into the print.
- **Tomorrow (Oct 23):** flash PMIs 09:45 ET, final Michigan sentiment 10:00 ET, AMEX and SLB before the open. **Monday Oct 26: VZ reports and the 2-year note auction.**

- This week has been a violent rotation *out* of AI/growth and *into* the average stock — and today was the day the market repriced the *cost* of AI.

- *Schwab:* **"Oil spiked and stocks and yields sagged after a report that the U.S. and Israel might resume attacks on Iran next month.
- Meta's heavy spending outlook and chip worries also hurt."**
- *Reuters (via businessday.co.za):* **"US stocks tumbled on Thursday, with the Nasdaq posting its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race."** The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index **-6.3%**,
- its biggest drop since 23 June.
- *IBKR:* **"Tech stocks are plunging as lackluster earnings reports spark AI slowdown worries with investors increasingly unsure about the return prospects of the massive investments."** Six of eleven sectors advanced;
- the curve bull-flattened aggressively, led by duration.

**5. After-hours earnings reactions**

**Meta (META) — Q3 2026, reported after the close → **-6.98% to $648.85** (regular session)**

- **This is the single most important item on the tape.** Yesterday META closed +0.47% and rose **+6.08% after hours** on the print; today it closed **-6.98%**.
- A ~13-point round trip in 24 hours on the same report.

- Per Reuters:
- Meta's results **beat** expectations, but the stock slid **7.5%** because it **posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade** due to AI-related expenditures, and **announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on AI**.
- The headline numbers themselves (revenue $64,601M +26%, ex-charge EPS $7.40 vs a $6.54–6.85 consensus, Q4 guide $73–76B) were good;
- the capital structure and cash-flow message was not, and **no 2027 capex number was given** against a Street pencil of ~$186B.

- *Schwab:* **"Another worry is continued heavy spending on AI and the third straight quarter of negative free cash flow."**
- The read-through is the market's: XLK -3.29%, XLC -1.42%, and the entire AI-capex complex down double digits in places.
- **Action item:** the Class C share issuance and the 2027 capex path are now the two open variables for the entire AI trade, not just for Meta.

**Moderna (MRNA) — **-17.57% to $202.63**, -2.21% after hours**

- **Partial Phase 3 INTerpath-001 data for intismeran autogene (Moderna/Merck's personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine) leaked online.** It appeared on Oncology Central and was **taken down shortly afterward**.
- The leaked partial data reported a **42% reduction in the risk of melanoma recurrence or death versus Keytruda alone**.
- Shares fell **as much as 25%** intraday; trading was **halted at 12:34 PM ET under a volatility-related LULD pause**;
- roughly $12 billion of market value erased (24/7 Wall St, measured at a -14.31% snapshot and an $84.9B cap).
- **The full data, released later on Thursday, appeared positive by Wall Street expectations**, and the formal company release described the recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival results as positive.
- Full presentation is at the **ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium this weekend in Madrid**.
- Merck -1.76%. A law firm (Frank R. Cruz) has opened a securities-fraud investigation into Moderna's disclosures.
- Also today: Moderna began a late-stage mRNA bird-flu vaccine trial, and the stock's Nasdaq-100 inclusion. ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/22/moderna-stock-cancer-vaccine-data-leak.html), [MarketWatch via Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20261022156/modernas-stock-tumbles-after-reported-leak-of-data-for-cancer-vaccine))
- **Watch:** Saturday's ESMO presentation is the event that resolves this.
- A leak-driven 17% drawdown on data that reads positive on the full release is a gap with a catalyst behind it.

**Nokia (NOK) — Q3 2026, reported before the open → **-14.81% to $7.88****

- **Beat on both lines and still collapsed.** Net sales **€5,154M (+10% reported, +9% cc)** vs €5.06B consensus; adjusted EPS **€0.102 vs €0.070** consensus.
- AI & Cloud net sales **+123%**, order intake **+118%**, €1.5B of new AI/cloud orders. Network Infrastructure +15% cc (IP Networks +43%, Optical +18%).
- Comparable operating profit +35% to €605M (11.7% margin). **2026 comparable operating profit outlook maintained at €2.1–2.6B.**
- **What broke it:** reported GAAP operating profit **-22% to €196M** on €357M of restructuring and integration charges; **full-year free-cash-flow conversion guidance cut to 35–55% from 55–75%**;
- **Q3 free cash flow negative at about -€99M**; 2026 restructuring charges now **€1.1B** with €800–900M of cash outflow, plus an extra **€400M** of working-capital investment.
- The stock broke below €7.50 and its 200-day SMA; €7.30 is the next support. Bernstein at Hold; at least one Buy with a $16 target.
- Infinera integration still on track for year-end 2026, a year ahead of plan.
- *This is the same pattern as Meta and Lam: a beat plus a cash-flow deterioration.* ([stocktitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/NOK/nokia-corporation-interim-report-for-q3-hghl6gapyb42.html), [investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-nokia-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4966766))

**Lam Research (LRCX) — day 2 of the collapse: **-11.76% to $230.15****

- Yesterday's beat-and-raise ($8.22B revenue vs $8.10B guided; non-GAAP EPS $2.20 vs $2.15 guided; Dec-quarter guide $8.60B) produced a -6.07% after-hours move;
- today the stock fell a further 5.7 points to close **-11.76%**, with the low at $227.68.
- The AI-capex complex sold it alongside AMD (-8.04%), INTC (-8.04%), AAOI (-11.96%) and the rest of the semiconductor equipment chain.

**8. Open research queue**

- **Meta's Class C / two-for-one non-voting share split.** A balance-sheet raise to fund AI is a regime change for the largest AI spender, and the whole complex read it as one.
- Get the structure (how many shares, at what price, what dilution) and whether the 2027 capex number was given or withheld on the 16:30 call.
- **Does the AI-capex repricing have more to give?** PHLX -6.3% (biggest since 23 June);
- TTMI -27.7%, FPS -21.5%, MXL -13.9%, ENTG -13.1%, VIAV -14.4%, UCTT -14.9%, FORM -15.3%, MPWR -9.0%, CRWV -10.1%, AAOI -12.0%.
- Which of these are earnings (TTMI, FPS, CRS reported) and which are pure beta? The 2027 WFE number from Lam's 17:00 call is the sector's anchor.
- **Moderna/ESMO.** The data that leaked and was pulled reads *positive* on the full release, and the stock is down 17.57% (~$12–14B of market value).
- Saturday's ESMO Presidential Symposium presentation is the catalyst — a re-rating setup or a confirmation of the leak interpretation. Also watch whether the securities-fraud investigation expands.
- **The "beat but cut cash flow" pattern.** Meta (first cash outflow in over a decade), Nokia (FCF conversion cut to 35–55% from 55–75%), Lam (guide implies +4.6% q/q after +22%).
- Three prints, one message: the market is now paying for cash conversion, not growth. Which of the week's remaining megacaps (MSFT 10-28, GOOGL/AMZN next week) carry the same exposure?
- **The oil/oil-inflation cross.** WTI +2.16% to $99.25 (high $100.17) on Houthi strikes on Saudi targets and a report that the US and Israel may resume strikes on Iran next month —
- while the 10-year fell 19.3bp. Two shocks pushing in opposite directions on nominal rates is an unusual configuration. Also:
- pre-market briefs put ~15% odds on an October 28 hike and ~87% by December (Cannon), while IBKR read the same decision as a pause given the loosening in financial conditions.
- **Those two readings conflict — the policy path is genuinely unsettled, not mispriced.**
- **Real yields vs the TIPS auction.** 5-yr TIPS stopped at 2.367%, the highest since October 2023, +41.2bp on the prior —
- with a 0.7bp tail and indirects down 5.8pts versus average. Implied 5-yr breakeven ~2.42%. Is the inflation compensation being rebuilt (oil) or the real curve being repriced (growth)?
- **Tomorrow's flash PMIs (09:45 ET).** The first hard read on whether the AI-capex scare is a valuation event or an orders event.
- LRCX, WDC and the memory chain are the transmission mechanism.
- **Is the breadth shift durable?** RSP on 184% of volume with a 1.91-point spread against SPY is the strongest breadth signal in weeks —
- but VIX 19.03 and the Dow/Russell futures flat suggest a rotation, not a regime change. Monday's tape resolves it.
- **BRZE/CRM deal spread** narrowed to ~3.6% ($45.86 vs the $47.50 cash price). With Salesforce's FY2028 close timeline, and the market in a risk-off mood, watch for arb widening.
- **Still open from yesterday:** Netflix's reported Q3 figures remain absent from indexed sources three days running;
- and the Meta 2027 capex path (see #1) is the single number that most of this tape now hangs on.
